borabora: All of French Polynesia, not only Bora Bora: the Society Islands (Tahiti, Moorea, Bora Bora, Raiatea, Huahine) and the Tuamotu atolls (Rangiroa, Fakarava, Tikehau), which are the main dive destinations. The place is the whole territory. Society Islands diving is day boats and lagoon snorkeling; the Tuamotu atolls are known for pass diving (strong currents through the channels into the lagoon, with grey reef sharks, dolphins and large schools). Regulated in-water swims with humpback whales are offered from Moorea and Tahiti, and at Rurutu in the Austral Islands, roughly August to October. Do not describe one lagoon as if it were the whole place.
komodo: Komodo National Park and the wider island of Flores: day boats and liveaboards from Labuan Bajo to the Komodo and Rinca island sites, plus other Flores dive areas (Riung, Maumere). The place is the island chain, not only the islands of the national park.
punta-cana: The whole Dominican Republic: Punta Cana and Bávaro on the east coast, Bayahibe (Catalina and Saona islands), La Romana, Sosúa and Cabarete on the north coast, Samaná, and the Santo Domingo coast (Boca Chica and its wrecks). Describe by area. Do not treat Punta Cana as the whole country.
havana: All of Cuba, not only Havana: Jardines de la Reina on the south coast (reached by liveaboard or floating hotel, known for sharks), María la Gorda and Cayo Levisa in the west, Playa Girón and Playa Larga (the Bay of Pigs, shore diving), Cayo Largo, Varadero and Guardalavaca. Describe the island, not the capital's seafront.
bagan: All of Myanmar, not the inland Bagan area: the Mergui (Myeik) Archipelago in the south (Burma Banks, Black Rock), reached mostly by liveaboard in a limited season of roughly October to May, and the Bay of Bengal beach coast (Ngapali, Ngwe Saung) with little diving.
whistler: Vancouver and Whistler. Diving is cold-water Pacific diving around Vancouver (Howe Sound and the Sunshine Coast approaches, with giant Pacific octopus, wolf eels and artificial-reef wrecks). Whistler itself is inland. Do not give a distance from Whistler or describe Vancouver relative to Whistler.
angkor: All of Cambodia, not the inland Angkor area: Koh Rong and Koh Rong Samloem off Sihanoukville, Koh Ta Kiev, and Kep and Kampot on the Gulf of Thailand coast. Short boat trips from the coast; the sea is calmest roughly November to May.
belfast-giants-causeway: All of Northern Ireland: the Causeway Coast and North Antrim, Rathlin Island (wrecks, seals, kelp), Strangford Lough and the Belfast Lough area. Cold-water diving.
snowdonia: All of Wales: Pembrokeshire (Skomer and Ramsey Island, grey seals), Anglesey and the Llŷn Peninsula, and Gower. Cold-water diving. Describe the sites by area, not by distance from any mountain or park.
banff: Banff and Jasper National Parks: very cold glacial lakes, chiefly Lake Minnewanka near Banff (a flooded former townsite, shore diving in drysuits). Nothing else is dived.
quebec-city: Quebec City and Montreal: cold, tidal St Lawrence River and Saguenay fjord diving (Tadoussac and the Saguenay, about three hours' drive from Quebec City), plus a few river sites near Montreal.
napa: Napa and Sonoma counties, the whole wine country (not the towns). The inland wine country has nothing to dive. The Sonoma County coast (Salt Point and Fort Ross) is a well-known cold-water kelp and abalone shore-diving area.
thailand: Phuket and the Andaman Coast: Phuket, Krabi, Phi Phi, Khao Lak, the Similan and Surin Islands and Richelieu Rock. Not the Gulf of Thailand islands (Koh Tao, Koh Samui), which are a different region.
